headline: Advance Planning for Coastal Camping and Long Beach Access
reservation: A National Park Entry Pass is required for all visitors, distinct from separate campsite or backcountry trekking bookings. The West Coast Trail requires a specific reservation system that often opens months in advance; always verify current procedures via Parks Canada for seasonal access changes. Traditional accommodations in Tofino and Ucluelet frequently require advance booking during the summer storm-watching and surfing seasons.

days.title: Ancient Rainforests and Coastal Sands

stops.name: Rainforest Trail
stops.detail: Walk the elevated wooden boardwalks through stands of massive Western Red Cedar and Sitka Spruce to observe the temperate rainforest ecosystem.

stops.name: Long Beach
stops.detail: Explore the vast expanse of sand between Tofino and Ucluelet, known for its surf culture and geological features like Incinerator Rock.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours for transit between trailheads; conditions vary by weather.
days.note: Boardwalks can be slippery when wet; maintain a steady pace on the loops.

days.title: Nu-chah-nulth Heritage and Inner Waters

stops.name: K<sup>w</sup>isitis Visitor Centre
stops.detail: Learn about the indigenous Nu-chah-nulth culture and the marine natural history of the Wickaninnish Beach area.

stops.name: Grice Bay
stops.detail: Visit this intertidal zone at high tide to observe the calm waters of the Clayoquot Sound UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for local road transfers; roads are winding.
days.note: Check tide tables locally as coastal access points change drastically with the water level.

days.title: Rocky Promontories and Marine Vistas

stops.name: Amphitrite Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: View the Wild Pacific Trail's rugged coastline where the open ocean meets the rocky shores of Vancouver Island.

stops.name: Schooner Cove
stops.detail: Hike through the forest to reach a secluded bay that showcases the transition from woodland to marine environment.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for travel between southern and northern park sections; conditions vary.
days.note: Stay on marked paths to avoid disturbing delicate coastal vegetation.

intel.title: Long Beach Congestion
intel.text: Parking lots at popular beach access points like Incinerator Rock fill early during summer months. Alternative lots may require a longer walk to the shoreline.

intel.title: Variable Coastal Coverage
intel.text: Cellular reception is intermittent along Highway 4 and within dense forest sections of the park. Carry physical maps for navigation between Tofino and Ucluelet.

intel.title: Gateway Service Stations
intel.text: Fuel is readily available in Tofino and Ucluelet, but services are sparse along the interior Highway 4 toward Port Alberni. Refill before entering the park reserve boundaries.

intel.title: Tidal Navigation
intel.text: Certain beach walks are only passable during low tide cycles. Consult the daily tide charts posted at visitor centers before departing for Schooner Cove.

intel.title: Seasonal Highway Conditions
intel.text: The Kennedy Hill section of Highway 4 may experience construction delays or winter weather restrictions. Check the DriveBC portal for the latest road status.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental vehicle at Nanaimo Airport (YCD) and stock up on supplies in Port Alberni before the mountain pass drive to the coast.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on unpaved logging roads nearby.
plan.goldenHour: Radar Hill for panoramic sunset views of the coast, noting that fog frequently obscures the horizon.
